questions.q: Which of the following statements is/are correct regarding the 'Instrument of Instructions' under the Government of India Act of 1935? 1️⃣ They were issued to the Governors and the Governor-General by the British Government. 2️⃣ The Directive Principles of State Policy are essentially a modern name for these instructions. 3️⃣ The fundamental difference is that DPSPs are addressed to the legislature and the executive of the State.

questions.q: "To promote international peace and security" is a Directive Principle under:
questions.e: Article 51, a Liberal-Intellectual principle, directs the state to promote international peace, security, and maintain just relations between nations.

questions.q: Under the 91st Amendment Act, 2003, a minister who is disqualified on the ground of defection shall:
o: Be ineligible to be appointed as a minister again for life.
Only be removed from his portfolio.
Be disqualified to be appointed as a minister until the expiry of his term or fresh election.
questions.e: The 91st Amendment specifies that a member disqualified for defection shall also be disqualified for appointment as a minister for the remainder of his term or until re-elected.

questions.q: "Participation of workers in management of industries" is provided under:
questions.e: Article 43A, added by the 42nd Amendment, directs the state to secure workers' participation in management.

questions.q: Regarding the Prime Minister's role in the 'Council of Ministers': 1️⃣ He is the head of the Council. 2️⃣ His death dissolves the Council. 3️⃣ He can dismiss the Council without the President's advice.
questions.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is incorrect; he can only advise the President to dismiss a minister or resign himself to collapse the council.

questions.q: Which DPSP directs the State to "protect and improve the environment"?
questions.e: Article 48A, added by the 42nd Amendment in 1976, directs the state to protect and improve the environment.

questions.q: The "Economic Affairs Committee" deals with: 1️⃣ Directing and coordinating government activities in the economic sphere. 2️⃣ Policy matters pertaining to foreign affairs. 3️⃣ Dealing with all policy matters pertaining to domestic affairs.
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct. Statements 2 and 3 are handled by the Political Affairs Committee.

questions.q: Which case established the 'Doctrine of Basic Structure'?
questions.e: In the Kesavananda Bharati case (1973), the SC established that Parliament cannot alter the basic structure of the Constitution.

questions.q: According to Article 74, there shall be a Council of Ministers with the Prime Minister at the head to:
o: Appoint the Chief Justice of India.
questions.e: Article 74(1) provides for the Council of Ministers to aid and advise the President.

questions.q: Which of the following is a Liberal-Intellectual principle?
questions.e: Article 44 is the only Liberal-Intellectual principle among the options.

questions.q: Regarding the "Appointments Committee of the Cabinet", which is correct? 1️⃣ It decides on higher level appointments in the Central Secretariat. 2️⃣ It is chaired by the Home Minister. 3️⃣ It deals with appointments to the three armed forces.
questions.e: Statement 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is incorrect as it is chaired by the PM.

questions.q: "The state shall endeavour to secure for the citizens a uniform civil code" is:
questions.e: This is the explicit text of Article 44.

questions.q: Who was the first woman to become a Cabinet Minister in India?
questions.e: Raj Kumari Amrit Kaur was the Health Minister in the first cabinet of independent India in 1947.

questions.q: "Collective Responsibility" means the Council of Ministers "sink or swim together". This is related to:
questions.e: This idiom describes the principle of collective responsibility embodied in Article 75.

questions.q: Which Article directs the State to "minimize inequalities in income, status, facilities, and opportunities"?
questions.e: Article 38(2), added by the 44th Amendment, contains this directive.

questions.q: The Prime Minister of India is:
questions.e: Under Article 75, the Prime Minister is appointed by the President.

questions.q: With reference to the 'Instrument of Instructions' under the Government of India Act of 1935, consider the following statements: 1️⃣ They were issued to the Governors and the Governor-General by the British Government. 2️⃣ The Directive Principles of State Policy are merely another name for these instructions. 3️⃣ The fundamental difference is that DPSPs are addressed to the legislature and the executive of the State.
questions.e: The Directive Principles resemble the ‘Instrument of Instructions’ enumerated in the Government of India Act of 1935. As Dr. B.R. Ambedkar stated, the only difference is that they are instructions to the legislature and the executive.

questions.q: Which of the following statements is/are correct regarding the 'Non-justiciable' nature of Directive Principles? 1️⃣ They are not legally enforceable by the courts for their violation. 2️⃣ The Constitution makes them fundamental in the governance of the country. 3️⃣ It is the moral obligation of the State authorities to apply them in making laws.
questions.e: Directive Principles are non-justiciable, meaning they are not legally enforceable by the courts for their violation. However, Article 37 declares that these principles are fundamental in the governance of the country and it shall be the duty of the State to apply them in making laws.

questions.q: Consider the following statements about the classification of Directive Principles: 1️⃣ Socialistic Principles aim at providing social and economic justice. 2️⃣ Gandhian Principles are based on the programme of reconstruction during the national movement. 3️⃣ Liberal-Intellectual Principles represent the ideology of liberalism.
questions.e: The principles are classified into three broad categories: Socialistic, which aim at providing social and economic justice; Gandhian, based on the national movement's reconstruction programme ; and Liberal-Intellectual, representing liberalism.

questions.q: Which of the following Socialistic Directive Principles is/are correct? 1️⃣ Article 39: To secure the right to adequate means of livelihood for all citizens. 2️⃣ Article 41: To secure the right to work, education, and public assistance in certain cases. 3️⃣ Article 42: To make provision for just and humane conditions of work and maternity relief.
questions.e: These are all Socialistic principles: Article 39 focuses on livelihood , Article 41 on the right to work and education , and Article 42 on humane work conditions and maternity relief.

questions.q: Regarding the 'Gandhian Principles', which of the following is/are explicitly mentioned in the DPSP? 1️⃣ To organize village panchayats (Article 40). 2️⃣ To promote cottage industries in rural areas (Article 43). 3️⃣ To promote the educational and economic interests of SCs, STs, and other weaker sections (Article 46).
questions.e: All these are Gandhian principles: Article 40 for village panchayats , Article 43 for cottage industries , and Article 46 for the interests of SCs, STs, and weaker sections.

questions.q: Consider the following statements regarding 'Liberal-Intellectual' principles: 1️⃣ Article 44: Uniform Civil Code for the citizens. 2️⃣ Article 50: Separation of judiciary from executive in public services. 3️⃣ Article 51: Promotion of international peace and security.
questions.e: These fall under the Liberal-Intellectual category: Article 44 for a Uniform Civil Code , Article 50 for separating judiciary and executive , and Article 51 for international peace.

questions.q: Which of the following Directive Principles were added by the 42nd Amendment Act of 1976? 1️⃣ Article 39: To secure opportunities for healthy development of children. 2️⃣ Article 39A: To promote equal justice and provide free legal aid to the poor. 3️⃣ Article 43A: To take steps to secure the participation of workers in management. 4️⃣ Article 48A: To protect and improve the environment.
questions.e: The 42nd Amendment Act of 1976 added four new Directive Principles: Article 39 (opportunities for children), Article 39A (free legal aid), Article 43A (workers' participation), and Article 48A (environment protection).

questions.q: With reference to the 'Conflict between Fundamental Rights and Directive Principles', consider the following: 1️⃣ In the Champakam Dorairajan case, the SC ruled that DPSPs are subsidiary to Fundamental Rights. 2️⃣ The 25th Amendment Act gave primacy to Articles 39(b) and 39(c) over Articles 14, 19, and 31. 3️⃣ In the Minerva Mills case, the SC declared that DPSPs have absolute primacy over all Fundamental Rights.
questions.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: the SC initially made DPSPs subsidiary , and the 25th Amendment gave primacy to Article 39(b) and (c). Statement 3 is incorrect because the Minerva Mills case struck down the provision giving DPSPs primacy over all FRs, emphasizing a balance instead.

questions.q: Which Constitutional Amendment Act made a provision for the State to provide early childhood care and education for all children until they complete the age of six years?
questions.e: The 86th Amendment Act of 2002 changed the subject matter of Article 45, directing the State to provide early childhood care and education up to age six.

questions.q: Consider the following statements about the 'Sanctions' behind DPSP: 1️⃣ The real force behind them is political (public opinion). 2️⃣ Sir B.N. Rau recommended that the rights of an individual should be divided into justiciable and non-justiciable. 3️⃣ They are intended to be the 'basis of all future legislation' in the country.
questions.e: The DPSP's primary sanction is the moral force of public opinion. The classification into justiciable and non-justiciable was recommended by Sir B.N. Rau. The Constituent Assembly intended them to be the basis of future governance.

questions.q: Regarding the 'Prime Minister' of India, which of the following statements is/are correct? 1️⃣ He is the head of the State. 2️⃣ He is the head of the Government. 3️⃣ The Constitution requires that he must be a member of the Lok Sabha at the time of appointment.
questions.e: The Prime Minister is the head of the Government, while the President is the head of the State. Statement 3 is incorrect because a person who is not a member of either House can be appointed PM for six months.

questions.q: With reference to the appointment of the Prime Minister, consider the following statements: 1️⃣ When no party has a clear majority, the President may exercise personal discretion. 2️⃣ The President usually appoints the leader of the largest party or coalition as the PM. 3️⃣ The PM must prove his majority in the Lok Sabha before taking the oath of office.
questions.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct regarding the President's discretionary power in a "hung Parliament". Statement 3 is incorrect; the SC has ruled the President can appoint a PM and then ask them to prove the majority within a reasonable period.

questions.q: Consider the following regarding the Prime Minister’s powers in relation to the Council of Ministers: 1️⃣ He advises the President on the appointment of other ministers. 2️⃣ He can dismiss a minister directly without advising the President. 3️⃣ His resignation or death leads to the automatic dissolution of the council of ministers.
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct as the President appoints ministers only on PM's advice. Statement 2 is incorrect; the PM advises the President to dismiss a minister. Statement 3 is correct; since the PM is the head, his exit collapses the entire council.

questions.q: Which of the following is/are the duties of the Prime Minister as per Article 78? 1️⃣ To communicate all decisions of the council of ministers to the President. 2️⃣ To furnish such information relating to the administration of the affairs of the Union as the President may call for. 3️⃣ To submit for consideration of the council any matter on which a decision has been taken by a minister but not considered by the council, if the President so requires.
questions.e: All three points are explicitly listed as the PM's duties towards the President under Article 78.

questions.q: With reference to the 'Central Council of Ministers', consider the following statements: 1️⃣ Article 74 deals with the status of the council. 2️⃣ Article 75 deals with the appointment, tenure, and responsibility of ministers. 3️⃣ The council of ministers is collectively responsible to the Parliament.
questions.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is incorrect; according to Article 75, the council of ministers is collectively responsible specifically to the Lok Sabha (the House of the People), not the entire Parliament.

questions.q: Under Article 74, the advice tendered by the Council of Ministers to the President: 1️⃣ Shall be inquired into by any court. 2️⃣ Is binding on the President after the 42nd and 44th Amendment Acts. 3️⃣ The President may require the council to reconsider such advice.
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect; Article 74(2) states that the advice shall not be inquired into by any court. Statements 2 and 3 are correct: the 42nd Amendment made the advice binding, and the 44th Amendment added that the President can ask for reconsideration.

questions.q: What is the maximum strength of the Union Council of Ministers as per the 91st Amendment Act, 2003?
o: 10% of the total strength of Parliament.
10% of the total strength of Lok Sabha.
15% of the total strength of Lok Sabha.
15% of the total strength of Parliament.
questions.e: The 91st Amendment Act of 2003 provided that the total number of ministers, including the PM, in the Central Council of Ministers shall not exceed 15% of the total strength of the Lok Sabha.

questions.q: Consider the following statements regarding the 'Collective Responsibility' of ministers: 1️⃣ It is the fundamental principle of the parliamentary system. 2️⃣ All ministers own joint responsibility to the Lok Sabha for all their acts of omission and commission. 3️⃣ A no-confidence motion passed against the council requires all ministers, including those from Rajya Sabha, to resign.
questions.e: Collective responsibility means the council acts as a team. If the Lok Sabha passes a no-confidence motion, the entire ministry must resign.

questions.q: With reference to the 'Individual Responsibility' of ministers, which of the following is/are correct? 1️⃣ Article 75 contains the principle of individual responsibility. 2️⃣ It means that the ministers hold office during the pleasure of the President. 3️⃣ The President can remove a minister only on the advice of the Prime Minister.
questions.e: All statements are correct. Article 75 states ministers hold office during the President's pleasure. In practice, the PM can advise the President to dismiss them.

questions.q: Which of the following best describes the 'Legal Responsibility' of ministers in India?
o: Courts can inquire into the legal advice given by ministers.
Ministers are legally responsible for every public act of the President.
The Constitution of India does not provide for a system of legal responsibility of a minister.
Every order of the President for a public act must be countersigned by a minister.
questions.e: Unlike Britain, India has no provision for legal responsibility of a minister. The courts are also barred from inquiring into the advice given to the President.

questions.q: Consider the following statements regarding the 'Cabinet': 1️⃣ It is a smaller body consisting of 15 to 20 ministers. 2️⃣ It was not mentioned in the original text of the Constitution. 3️⃣ It was inserted in Article 352 by the 44th Amendment Act of 1978.
questions.e: All statements are correct. The Cabinet is the inner core of the Council of Ministers. The word was added to the Constitution via the 44th Amendment.

questions.q: What is the "Super-Cabinet" according to the text?
questions.e: The Political Affairs Committee is often described as a "Super-Cabinet" because it deals with all policy matters.

questions.q: Regarding 'Cabinet Committees', consider the following statements: 1️⃣ They are extra-constitutional in emergence. 2️⃣ They are of two types: standing and ad hoc. 3️⃣ They are always chaired by the Prime Minister.
questions.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is incorrect; while the PM chairs most, some are chaired by other ministers.

questions.q: Which of the following is/are the roles of the 'Cabinet'? 1️⃣ It is the highest decision-making authority in our politico-administrative system. 2️⃣ It is the supreme direction-controlling body of the Central government. 3️⃣ it is the chief policy-formulating body of the Central government.
questions.e: The Cabinet performs all these roles as the top-tier executive body.

questions.q: With reference to the 'Kitchen Cabinet', which of the following is/are correct? 1️⃣ It is a formal constitutional body. 2️⃣ It consists of the PM and two to four influential colleagues. 3️⃣ It can include outsiders like family members or friends of the Prime Minister.
questions.e: The Kitchen Cabinet is an informal, extra-constitutional body. It usually consists of a few close colleagues and may include non-ministers.

questions.q: Consider the following statements regarding the "Shadow Cabinet": 1️⃣ It is a unique institution of the British cabinet system. 2️⃣ It is formed by the opposition party to prepare its members for future ministerial office. 3️⃣ There is no such institution in India.
questions.e: All statements are correct. The Shadow Cabinet is a British concept; it does not exist in the Indian system.

questions.q: Which of the following Directive Principles are based on 'Liberal-Intellectual' ideology? 1️⃣ To secure a uniform civil code for all citizens (Article 44). 2️⃣ To provide early childhood care and education for all children (Article 45). 3️⃣ To separate the judiciary from the executive (Article 50). 4️⃣ To promote cottage industries (Article 43).
questions.e: Articles 44, 45, and 50 are Liberal-Intellectual. Article 43 (cottage industries) is a Gandhian principle.

questions.q: According to Article 39(f), the State shall direct its policy towards securing:
o: That children are given opportunities and facilities to develop in a healthy manner.
questions.e: Article 39(f) specifically directs the state to secure opportunities for the healthy development of children.

questions.q: With reference to the 'Directives Outside Part IV', Article 351 deals with:
o: Claims of SCs and STs to services.
Instruction in mother tongue at primary stage.
questions.e: Article 351, located in Part XVII, directs the Union to promote the spread of the Hindi language.

questions.q: In which case did the Supreme Court hold that "Fundamental Rights are not sacrosanct and can be amended by the Parliament"?
questions.e: In the Kesavananda Bharati case (1973), the SC held that Parliament can amend any part of the Constitution, including FRs.

questions.q: Which of the following statements regarding the "Board of Control" is/are correct? 1️⃣ It was created by Pitt’s India Act of 1784 to manage political affairs. 2️⃣ It was empowered to supervise all operations of the civil and military government of the British possessions. 3️⃣ It was abolished by the Government of India Act of 1858.
questions.e: All statements are correct. The Board of Control was established in 1784 , given supervisory powers , and abolished in 1858.

questions.q: With reference to the 'Regulating Act of 1773', which of the following is correct?
o: It abolished the Court of Directors.
It designated the Governor of Bengal as 'Governor-General of Bengal'.
It provided for the establishment of a Federal Court.
It made the Governors of Bombay and Madras independent of Bengal.
questions.e: The Act designated the Governor of Bengal as the 'Governor-General of Bengal'.

questions.q: Consider the following regarding the 'Charter Act of 1833': 1️⃣ It was the final step towards centralisation in British India. 2️⃣ It made Lord William Bentick the first Governor-General of India. 3️⃣ It deprived the Governors of Bombay and Madras of their legislative powers.
questions.e: All statements are correct. This act was the final step in centralisation and appointed Bentick as the first GG of India.

questions.q: The 'Macaulay Committee' (1854) was related to which of the following?
questions.e: The Macaulay Committee was the Committee on the Indian Civil Service, appointed in 1854.

questions.q: With reference to the 'Government of India Act of 1858', which of the following is/are correct? 1️⃣ It changed the designation of Governor-General of India to Viceroy of India. 2️⃣ Lord Canning became the first Viceroy. 3️⃣ It created a 15-member Council of India to assist the Secretary of State.
questions.e: All statements are correct features of the 1858 Act.

questions.q: Which Act introduced the system of 'communal representation' for Muslims for the first time?
questions.e: The Indian Councils Act of 1909 introduced separate electorates for Muslims.

questions.q: Regarding the 'Government of India Act of 1919', consider the following statements: 1️⃣ It introduced bicameralism and direct elections for the first time. 2️⃣ It divided provincial subjects into transferred and reserved. 3️⃣ It provided for the establishment of a Central Public Service Commission.
questions.e: All statements are correct. The Act introduced bicameralism and provincial dyarchy.

questions.q: Which of the following features belong to the 'Government of India Act of 1935'? 1️⃣ Establishment of an All-India Federation. 2️⃣ Abolition of dyarchy in the provinces. 3️⃣ Establishment of the Reserve Bank of India. 4️⃣ Creation of a Federal Court.
questions.e: All these were major provisions of the 1935 Act.

questions.q: The 'Poona Pact' (1932) was an agreement between:
o: Muslim League and the British Government.
questions.e: The Poona Pact was an agreement between the Congress and Dr. B.R. Ambedkar.

questions.q: Consider the following statements regarding the 'Indian Independence Act of 1947': 1️⃣ It declared India as an independent and sovereign state from August 15, 1947. 2️⃣ It abolished the office of Viceroy. 3️⃣ It proclaimed the lapse of British paramountcy over Indian princely states.
questions.e: All these were key features of the 1947 Act.

questions.q: Who was the Chairman of the 'Union Constitution Committee'?
questions.e: Jawaharlal Nehru was the chairman of the Union Constitution Committee.

questions.q: Which of the following is/are 'Minor Committees' of the Constituent Assembly? 1️⃣ Credentials Committee 2️⃣ House Committee 3️⃣ Order of Business Committee 4️⃣ Steering Committee
questions.e: Steering Committee was a Major Committee. The others listed were Minor Committees.

questions.q: Consider the following statements regarding the 'Drafting Committee': 1️⃣ It was set up on August 29, 1947. 2️⃣ It consisted of seven members. 3️⃣ N. Madhava Rau replaced B.L. Mitter who resigned due to ill-health.
questions.e: All statements are correct.

questions.q: On which date was the Constitution of India 'Adopted, Enacted and Given to themselves' by the people?
questions.e: November 26, 1949, is the date of adoption.

questions.q: Which Article of the Constitution deals with the "Authoritative text in Hindi language"?
questions.e: Article 394A provides for an authoritative text of the Constitution in Hindi.

questions.q: With reference to 'Union and its Territory', consider the following statements: 1️⃣ The 'Territory of India' is a wider expression than the 'Union of India'. 2️⃣ The 'Union of India' includes only the States. 3️⃣ The 'Territory of India' includes States, Union Territories, and territories that may be acquired.
questions.e: The 'Territory of India' is a wider expression because the 'Union of India' includes only the states.

questions.q: Consider the following regarding Article 3 of the Constitution: 1️⃣ Parliament can form a new state by uniting a part of any state to any other state. 2️⃣ A bill for this purpose can be introduced only with the prior recommendation of the President. 3️⃣ The President must refer the bill to the state legislature for its binding opinion.
questions.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is incorrect because the opinion of the state legislature is not binding.

questions.q: With reference to the 'Berubari Union' case (1960), the Supreme Court held that:
o: Indian territory can be ceded to a foreign state only by amending the Constitution under Article 368.
Settlement of boundary disputes always requires a constitutional amendment.
Article 3 includes the power to diminish the area of India as a whole.
Parliament can cede Indian territory to a foreign country under Article 3.
questions.e: The SC held that ceding Indian territory requires a constitutional amendment under Article 368.

questions.q: Regarding the 'Evolution of States', which commission first recommended the reorganization of states on a linguistic basis?
questions.e: The Fazl Ali Commission broadly accepted language as the basis of reorganization.

questions.q: Which of the following pairs of 'State - Year of Creation' is NOT correctly matched?
questions.e: Nagaland was formed in 1963. Gujarat (1960), Haryana (1966), and Sikkim (1975) are correctly matched.

questions.q: Which of the following statements regarding the 'Union and Its Territory' is correct? 1️⃣ The 'Territory of India' is a wider expression than the 'Union of India' because it includes acquired territories. 2️⃣ The names of the States and Union Territories are mentioned in the Second Schedule. 3️⃣ Parliament can admit new states into the Union under Article 2.
questions.e: 'Territory of India' is a wider expression than 'Union of India' as the latter includes only states while the former includes states, UTs, and acquired territories. Names of States and UTs are in the First Schedule, not the Second. Article 2 empowers Parliament to admit or establish new states.

questions.q: With reference to Parliament's power to reorganize states under Article 3, consider the following: 1️⃣ Parliament can increase the area of any state but cannot diminish it. 2️⃣ A bill for state reorganization can be introduced only on the recommendation of the President. 3️⃣ The President is bound by the views expressed by the state legislature regarding the bill.
questions.e: Under Article 3, Parliament can both increase and diminish the area of any state. A bill requires the President's prior recommendation. However, the views of the state legislature are not binding on the President or Parliament.

questions.q: The 'Dhar Commission' and 'JVP Committee' were appointed to examine the reorganization of states on the basis of:
questions.e: Both the Dhar Commission (1948) and the JVP Committee (1948) were appointed to examine the feasibility of reorganizing states on a linguistic basis. Both initially rejected language as the basis.

questions.q: Which of the following was the first linguistic state created in India?
questions.e: In October 1953, the Government of India was forced to create the first linguistic state, known as Andhra State, by separating Telugu-speaking areas from the Madras State.

questions.q: Regarding the 'Citizenship' provisions in the Constitution, which of the following is/are correct? 1️⃣ Article 5 deals with citizenship at the commencement of the Constitution. 2️⃣ No person shall be a citizen of India if he/she voluntarily acquires foreign citizenship. 3️⃣ The Parliament has the power to make any provision with respect to the acquisition of citizenship.
questions.e: Article 5 identifies citizens at the start of the Constitution. Article 9 states that voluntary acquisition of foreign citizenship terminates Indian citizenship. Article 11 gives Parliament the power to regulate citizenship by law.

questions.q: Under the Citizenship Act of 1955, which of the following is NOT a way of losing Indian citizenship?
questions.e: The Citizenship Act (1955) prescribes three ways of losing citizenship: renunciation, termination, and deprivation. Incarceration is a ground for deprivation only if it occurs within five years of registration/naturalisation.

questions.q: With reference to the 'Overseas Citizen of India (OCI) Cardholder' scheme, consider the following: 1️⃣ It was introduced by merging the PIO and OCI schemes in 2015. 2️⃣ OCI cardholders enjoy parity with Indian citizens in the matter of right to public employment. 3️⃣ Citizens of Pakistan and Bangladesh are ineligible for this scheme.
questions.e: The PIO and OCI schemes were merged in 2015. OCI cardholders are specifically *not* entitled to equality of opportunity in public employment (Article 16). Persons who have been citizens of Pakistan or Bangladesh are ineligible.

questions.q: Which of the following is/are included in the definition of 'State' under Article 12? 1️⃣ Executive and legislative organs of the Union government. 2️⃣ All local authorities like municipalities and panchayats. 3️⃣ Statutory or non-statutory authorities like LIC and SAIL.
questions.e: Article 12 defines 'State' to include the Union and State governments/legislatures, local authorities, and all other statutory or non-statutory authorities.

questions.q: Article 13 of the Constitution is significant because it:
o: Lists the duties of the Prime Minister.
Expressively provides for the doctrine of judicial review.
Empowers the President to issue ordinances.
questions.e: Article 13 declares that all laws inconsistent with or in derogation of Fundamental Rights shall be void, thereby expressively providing for judicial review.

questions.q: Consider the following regarding 'Rule of Law' as propounded by A.V. Dicey: 1️⃣ It implies the absence of arbitrary power. 2️⃣ It denotes equality before the law. 3️⃣ In the Indian system, the Constitution is the source of individual rights.
questions.e: Dicey's concept includes the absence of arbitrary power and equality before the law. While Dicey argued the Constitution results from individual rights, in India, the Constitution is the *source* of those rights.

questions.q: Which of the following is an exception to the 'Equality before Law' (Article 14)?
o: Foreign sovereigns and ambassadors enjoy immunity from civil and criminal proceedings.
The President of India is not answerable to any court for the exercise of his powers.
A member of Parliament is not liable to any proceedings for anything said in Parliament.
questions.e: Exceptions include Article 361 for the President/Governors, Article 105 for MP immunity, and international law for foreign diplomats.

questions.q: Article 15(2) prohibits discrimination against citizens regarding access to shops, restaurants, and public resorts by:
o: Both the State and private individuals.
Neither, it is a non-binding directive.
questions.e: Article 15(2) prohibits discrimination by both the State and private individuals regarding access to public places.

questions.q: The 93rd Amendment Act (2005) added a provision to Article 15 to enable reservation for:
questions.e: The 93rd Amendment Act added Article 15(5), empowering the State to make special provisions for socially and educationally backward classes regarding admission to educational institutions.

questions.q: Regarding 'Equality of Opportunity in Public Employment' (Article 16), which of the following is correct? 1️⃣ No citizen can be discriminated against for any office under the State on grounds of residence. 2️⃣ Parliament can prescribe residence as a requirement for certain appointments. 3️⃣ The State can provide reservation for any backward class not adequately represented in services.
questions.e: Article 16 prohibits discrimination on various grounds including residence. However, Article 16(3) allows Parliament to prescribe residence requirements. Article 16(4) allows for reservations for under-represented backward classes.

questions.q: In the Indra Sawhney case (1992), the Supreme Court ruled that the total reserved quota should not exceed:
questions.e: The Supreme Court held that the total reserved quota should not exceed 50% except in some extraordinary situations.

questions.q: With reference to the 'Abolition of Untouchability', consider the following: 1️⃣ Article 17 abolishes 'untouchability' and forbids its practice. 2️⃣ The term 'untouchability' is defined in the Protection of Civil Rights Act, 1955. 3️⃣ The right under Article 17 is available against private individuals.
questions.e: Article 17 abolishes the practice. The term is *not* defined in the Constitution or the Act. The SC held this right is available against private individuals.

questions.q: Article 18 abolishes titles. Which of the following is/are correct in this regard? 1️⃣ It prohibits the State from conferring any title except military or academic distinctions. 2️⃣ A citizen of India cannot accept any title from any foreign state. 3️⃣ National awards like Bharat Ratna are not 'titles' within the meaning of Article 18.
questions.e: Article 18 bans the State from conferring titles other than military/academic. Citizens cannot accept foreign titles. The SC ruled that National Awards do not amount to 'titles'.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT one of the six rights guaranteed by Article 19?
o: Right to acquire, hold and dispose of property.
questions.e: The right to acquire, hold, and dispose of property was deleted from Article 19 by the 44th Amendment Act of 1978.

questions.q: Protection in respect of conviction for offences (Article 20) includes: 1️⃣ No ex-post-facto law. 2️⃣ No double jeopardy. 3️⃣ No self-incrimination.
questions.e: Article 20 provides these three specific protections to an accused person.

questions.q: Consider the following statements regarding Article 21: 1️⃣ No person shall be deprived of his life or personal liberty except according to procedure established by law. 2️⃣ The Supreme Court in the Maneka case (1978) introduced the 'due process of law' concept. 3️⃣ It protects only against arbitrary executive action and not legislative action.
questions.e: Article 21 guarantees life and liberty according to legal procedure. The Maneka case introduced 'due process', making protection available against both arbitrary executive and legislative action.

questions.q: Article 21-A, which makes elementary education a Fundamental Right for children aged 6-14, was added by the:
questions.e: The 86th Constitutional Amendment Act of 2002 added Article 21-A to achieve 'Education for All'.

questions.q: With reference to 'Preventive Detention' (Article 22), which of the following is correct?
o: It is a punitive measure after a trial.
Parliament has exclusive authority for reasons connected with defense, foreign affairs, and security.
It is a common feature in most democratic constitutions globally.
It can be used to detain a person for more than three months without any advisory board review.
questions.e: Preventive detention is a precautionary measure based on suspicion. It cannot exceed 3 months without an advisory board report. Parliament has exclusive power for defense/foreign affairs reasons. India is the only democratic country with such an integral constitutional provision.

questions.q: Article 23 of the Constitution prohibits:
o: Traffic in human beings and forced labour.
questions.e: Article 23 prohibits traffic in human beings, 'begar', and other similar forms of forced labour.

questions.q: Article 24 prohibits the employment of children below the age of 14 years in:
questions.e: Article 24 prohibits child labor in factories, mines, or other hazardous activities.

questions.q: Consider the following regarding 'Freedom of Religion' (Article 25): 1️⃣ It includes the right to propagate one's religion. 2️⃣ The right to propagate includes the right to convert another person. 3️⃣ It is subject to public order, morality, and health.
questions.e: Article 25 includes the right to propagate tenets. However, it does *not* include the right to convert another person, as that impinges on others' freedom of conscience. It is subject to public order, morality, and health.

questions.q: Article 26 protects the 'Collective Freedom of Religion' by allowing religious denominations to: 1️⃣ Manage their own affairs in matters of religion. 2️⃣ Own and acquire movable and immovable property. 3️⃣ Administer such property in accordance with law.
questions.e: Article 26 guarantees these specific rights to every religious denomination or its section.

questions.q: Under Article 27, the State is prohibited from:
o: Spending public money collected via tax for the promotion of any particular religion.
questions.e: Article 27 states that no person shall be compelled to pay taxes for the promotion or maintenance of any particular religion. It prohibits tax use but not the levy of fees.

questions.q: Regarding Article 28, in which type of educational institution is religious instruction completely prohibited?
o: Institutions administered by the State but established under a trust.
Institutions receiving aid from the State.
Institutions wholly maintained by the State.
questions.e: Religious instruction is strictly prohibited in institutions 100% maintained out of State funds.

questions.q: Article 29 provides that any section of citizens residing in India has the right to:
o: Conserve their distinct language, script, or culture.
questions.e: Article 29 gives any section of citizens (minority or majority) the right to conserve their distinct language, script, or culture.

questions.q: Under Article 30, minorities (religious or linguistic) have the right to: 1️⃣ Establish and administer educational institutions of their choice. 2️⃣ Not be discriminated against in matters of state aid. 3️⃣ Impart education to their children in their own language.
questions.e: All these are rights granted to minorities under Article 30.

questions.q: Which Article was described by Dr. Ambedkar as "the heart and soul of the Constitution"?
questions.e: Dr. Ambedkar called Article 32 the most important article because it provides the right to move the Supreme Court for the enforcement of Fundamental Rights.

questions.q: The writ of 'Mandamus' literally means:
questions.e: Mandamus is a Latin term meaning 'we command', issued to a public official to perform their duties.

questions.q: Which writ is issued by a higher court to a lower court to *prevent* the latter from exceeding its jurisdiction?
questions.e: Prohibition is issued to forbid a lower court from exceeding or usurping jurisdiction.

questions.q: The writ of 'Quo-Warranto' is used to:
o: Quash an order of a tribunal.
Inquire into the legality of a person's claim to a public office.
Compel a public official to act.
Release a person from illegal detention.
questions.e: Quo-Warranto (literally 'by what authority') prevents the illegal usurpation of a public office.

questions.q: Article 33 empowers the Parliament to restrict or abrogate the Fundamental Rights of: 1️⃣ Members of the armed forces. 2️⃣ Police forces and intelligence agencies. 3️⃣ Non-combatant employees of the armed forces like cooks and barbers.
questions.e: Article 33 allows Parliament to restrict FRs for armed forces, police, and analogous services, including non-combatant employees, to ensure discipline.

questions.q: 'Martial Law' in India:
o: Can only be declared on grounds of 'armed rebellion'.
Is defined explicitly in the Constitution.
Suspends ordinary law and the government by military tribunals.
Is the same as a National Emergency.
questions.e: Martial law means 'military rule' and implies the suspension of ordinary law. It is not defined in the Constitution and differs from National Emergency.

questions.q: According to Article 35, the power to make laws to give effect to certain specified Fundamental Rights vests only in:
questions.e: To ensure uniformity across the country, Article 35 vests the law-making power for specified FRs solely in the Parliament.

questions.q: Which Article was added by the 1st Amendment (1951) to protect land reform laws from being challenged on FR grounds?
questions.e: Article 31A was added to save specific categories of laws, like those related to land reforms, from being invalidated based on Articles 14 and 19.

questions.q: The 'Ninth Schedule' was added to the Constitution to:
o: Allocate seats in the Rajya Sabha.
Protect certain acts and regulations from judicial review.
List the official languages of India.
Define the powers of the Panchayats.
questions.e: The Ninth Schedule, along with Article 31B, was added by the 1st Amendment to immunize laws included in it from Fundamental Rights challenges.

questions.q: In the Minerva Mills case (1980), the Supreme Court held that 'Judicial Review' is a:
questions.e: The Supreme Court struck down provisions of the 42nd Amendment and reaffirmed that judicial review is a basic feature.

questions.q: Which of the following is correct regarding the 'Directive Principles of State Policy' (DPSP)?
o: They are fundamental in the governance of the country.
They are legally enforceable by the courts.
They were borrowed from the American Constitution.
questions.e: Article 37 declares that while non-justiciable, DPSPs are fundamental in governance. They were borrowed from the Irish Constitution and aim to establish social and economic democracy.

questions.q: Which of the following DPSPs is based on the ideology of 'Socialism'?
o: Equal pay for equal work for both men and women.
questions.e: Article 39(d) for equal pay is a socialistic principle. Village panchayats (Art 40) and cottage industries (Art 43) are Gandhian. Uniform Civil Code (Art 44) is Liberal-Intellectual.

questions.q: Article 40 of the Directive Principles directs the State to:
questions.e: Article 40 directs the state to organize village panchayats and endow them with necessary powers.

questions.q: The 'Uniform Civil Code' for citizens is mentioned under:
questions.e: Article 44 directs the State to secure for citizens a uniform civil code throughout India.

questions.q: Which Directive Principle was added by the 97th Amendment Act of 2011?
questions.e: The 97th Amendment added Article 43B regarding the promotion of co-operative societies.

questions.q: Consider the following regarding the Prime Minister of India: 1️⃣ He is appointed by the President. 2️⃣ He chooses his ministers and the President appoints them on his advice. 3️⃣ He can be a member of any of the two Houses of Parliament.
questions.e: Under Article 75, the PM is appointed by the President. The PM selects the team and can belong to either Lok Sabha or Rajya Sabha.

questions.q: In 1997, the Supreme Court ruled that a person who is not a member of either House can be appointed as Prime Minister for:
questions.e: A person can be PM or a minister for six consecutive months without being a member of Parliament, after which they must be elected or cease holding office.

questions.q: The Prime Minister is the ex-officio chairman of which of the following? 1️⃣ NITI Aayog. 2️⃣ National Integration Council. 3️⃣ Inter-State Council. 4️⃣ National Water Resources Council.
questions.e: The Prime Minister chairs all these major national bodies.

questions.q: According to Article 75, the Council of Ministers is collectively responsible to:
questions.e: Collective responsibility means the Council is responsible specifically to the House of the People (Lok Sabha).

questions.q: Which Cabinet Committee is often described as the "Super-Cabinet"?
questions.e: The Political Affairs Committee is the most powerful cabinet committee, dealing with all domestic and foreign policy matters.

questions.q: Regarding 'Cabinet Committees', which of the following is correct? 1️⃣ They are extra-constitutional in emergence. 2️⃣ They are set up by the Prime Minister according to the exigencies of the time. 3️⃣ Their membership is restricted only to Cabinet Ministers.
questions.e: Cabinet Committees are not mentioned in the Constitution and are formed by the PM. While they usually include cabinet ministers, non-cabinet ministers can also be members.

questions.q: Which Prime Minister of India headed the first non-Congress government?
questions.e: Morarji Desai led the Janata Party government in 1977, the first non-Congress government at the Centre.

questions.q: Under Article 74, the advice tendered by the Council of Ministers to the President is:
o: Optional for the President to follow.
Inquired into by the High Courts.
Subject to approval by the Lok Sabha.
questions.e: The 42nd and 44th Amendments made the council's advice binding, though the President can ask for one-time reconsideration. Article 74(2) bars judicial inquiry into the advice.

questions.q: Which Article directs the State to "separate the judiciary from the executive in the public services"?
questions.e: Article 50 directs the state to take steps to separate the judiciary from the executive in public services.

questions.q: The 'Kitchen Cabinet' is:
o: A formal committee of the Parliament.
A group of ministers in charge of food security.
An informal body consisting of the PM and two to four influential colleagues.
questions.e: The 'Kitchen Cabinet' or 'Inner Cabinet' is an informal, extra-constitutional circle of advisors where real power often resides.

questions.q: Which Directive Principle targets "equal pay for equal work"?
questions.e: Article 39(d) directs the state to secure equal pay for equal work for both men and women.

questions.q: The 'Economic Affairs Committee' of the Cabinet is chaired by:
questions.e: The Prime Minister chairs the Economic Affairs Committee, which oversees government activities in the economic sphere.

questions.q: In which case did the Supreme Court hold that the Indian Constitution is founded on the bedrock of the balance between Fundamental Rights and Directive Principles?
questions.e: In the Minerva Mills case (1980), the SC emphasized that FRs and DPSPs are complementary and their balance is a basic feature.

questions.q: According to Article 78, who is the principal channel of communication between the President and the Council of Ministers?
questions.e: Article 78 lists the duties of the PM to keep the President informed about administrative affairs and decisions.

questions.q: Which of the following is correct regarding the 'Collective Responsibility' of ministers? 1️⃣ They sink or swim together. 2️⃣ They must defend cabinet decisions in the Parliament. 3️⃣ If a minister disagrees with a cabinet decision and is not prepared to defend it, he must resign.
questions.e: Collective responsibility requires a unified front; disagreement with cabinet decisions necessitating resignation.

questions.q: Which Act created the office of the 'Secretary of State for India'?
questions.e: The 1858 Act created the Secretary of State as a member of the British Cabinet with complete authority over Indian administration.

questions.q: The 'Macaulay Committee' (1854) was related to:
questions.e: The Macaulay Committee was the Committee on the Indian Civil Service.

questions.q: Which Act introduced 'Separate Electorates' for Muslims for the first time?
questions.e: The Indian Councils Act of 1909 (Morley-Minto Reforms) legalized communalism through separate electorates.

questions.q: Under the 1919 Act, 'Dyarchy' was introduced in:
questions.e: The Government of India Act of 1919 introduced dyarchy (double rule) at the provincial level.

questions.q: The 'Poona Pact' (1932) resulted in:
o: Reserved seats for depressed classes within the Hindu joint electorate.
questions.e: The Poona Pact between Congress and Dr. Ambedkar retained joint electorates but provided reserved seats for Scheduled Castes.

questions.q: Which Act for the first time called Company's territories 'British possessions in India'?
questions.e: Pitt's India Act of 1784 was significant for first using this specific terminology.

questions.q: The 'Instrument of Accession' was used by which state to join India?
questions.e: Kashmir joined the Indian Union through the Instrument of Accession.

questions.q: 'Viksit Bharat' targets India becoming a developed nation by:
questions.e: 2047 is the centenary of independence and the target year for developed status.

questions.q: Which Article is the 'Magna Carta' of India?
questions.e: Part III (Fundamental Rights) is described as the Magna Carta of India.

questions.q: The 'Creamy Layer' exclusion for OBC benefits was directed by the Supreme Court in the:
questions.e: In the Indra Sawhney (Mandal) case, the SC directed the government to exclude advanced sections among OBCs.

questions.q: 'Mission LiFE' was introduced to promote:
questions.e: Mission LiFE (Lifestyle for Environment) nudges individuals toward mindful utilization of resources.

questions.q: Which writ is the 'bulwark of individual liberty' against arbitrary detention?
questions.e: Habeas Corpus literally means 'to have the body of' and protects against illegal detention.

questions.q: 'SASCI' loans provided to states are for a tenure of:
questions.e: SASCI provides 50-year interest-free loans for capital investment in states.

questions.q: Which Article empowers Parliament to change the name or boundaries of states?
questions.e: Article 3 allows Parliament to redraw the internal map of India.

questions.q: The 'Economic Complexity Index' (ECI) measures:
o: The average age of the workforce.
Knowledge intensity of an economy's exports.
questions.e: ECI reflects the diversity and sophistication of an economy's productive knowledge.

questions.q: Which Fundamental Right prohibits 'Begar' and forced labor?
questions.e: Article 23 prohibits traffic in human beings and all forms of forced labor.

questions.q: The 'Account Aggregator' framework is regulated by:
questions.e: The Reserve Bank of India oversees the AA data-sharing ecosystem.

questions.q: 'BharatNet' project aims to connect:
o: All Gram Panchayats with optical fiber.
questions.e: BharatNet is the rural broadband connectivity program using optical fiber.

questions.q: Which Article abolishes 'Untouchability'?
questions.e: Article 17 abolishes it and makes its practice a punishable offence.

questions.q: The 'Nowcasting' model matured into a reliable tool after:
questions.e: After three years of operational use, the DEA now uses it for real-time growth assess.

questions.q: Which meeting of the GST Council introduced the revised two-rate structure?
questions.e: The 56th GST Council meeting rationalized the rates into 5% and 18%.

questions.q: 'PM-JANMAN' mission addresses the needs of:
questions.e: It targets socio-economic development for Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Groups.

questions.q: Which Fundamental Right protects the 'wearing and carrying of kirpans'?
questions.e: Article 25 includes an explanation that wearing/carrying kirpans is part of the Sikh profession.

questions.q: 'Sagar Mala' is an initiative for:
questions.e: Sagar Mala modernization targets improving coastal infrastructure and logistics.

questions.q: Which Article is called the 'soul' of the Constitution?
questions.e: Dr. Ambedkar called Article 32 the very soul and heart of the Constitution.

questions.q: The 'VBSA Bill' aims to grant autonomy to:
questions.e: The Viksit Bharat Shiksha Adhishthan Bill targets top-tier university autonomy.

questions.q: India leads the world in the production of:
questions.e: India holds the top global rank in milk and pulses production.

questions.q: 'Mission Shakti' sub-scheme 'Sambal' is for:
questions.e: Sambal is the component of Mission Shakti dedicated to women's safety.

questions.q: The 'Account Aggregator' allows data sharing based on:
questions.e: The AA system is entirely digital and requires explicit user consent.

questions.q: Which Constitutional Amendment added 'Fundamental Duties'?
questions.e: Fundamental Duties (Article 51-A) were added in 1976 based on the Swaran Singh Committee.

questions.q: Regarding 'Directive Principles', which of the following is correct? 1️⃣ They are instructions to the State. 2️⃣ They are non-justiciable. 3️⃣ They are fundamental in governance.
questions.e: DPSPs are constitutional instructions, non-justiciable, but fundamental in the governance of the country.

questions.q: Which socialistic principle targets the "healthy development of children"?
questions.e: Article 39(f) directs the state to secure opportunities for the healthy development of children.

questions.q: 'PM-KUSUM' scheme aims to:
questions.e: PM-KUSUM targets energy security for farmers through solar power.

questions.q: Which Article deals with the 'Conduct of Business' of the Government?
questions.e: Article 77 specifies that all executive actions shall be taken in the name of the President.

questions.q: The 'Entrepreneurial State' manages uncertainty through:
questions.e: An entrepreneurial state acts before certainty emerges and learns from course corrections.

questions.q: Which Article directs the state to "promote international peace"?
questions.e: Article 51 focuses on international relations and world peace.

questions.q: 'Individual Responsibility' under Article 75 means ministers hold office during the pleasure of:
questions.e: Article 75 explicitly states that ministers hold office during the pleasure of the President.

questions.q: Which Act renamed 'United Provinces' to 'Uttar Pradesh'?
questions.e: The United Provinces was the first state to be renamed in 1950.

questions.q: 'NIPUN Bharat' targets foundational literacy by:
questions.e: NIPUN Bharat ensures every child achieves foundational skills by the end of Grade 3.

questions.q: The 44th Amendment added a provision to Article 38 to:
o: Minimize inequalities in income and status.
questions.e: The 44th Amendment Act (1978) added Article 38(2) to minimize inequalities.
